record.paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
record.original_question: Let X be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and let T be a bounded linear operator on X. Is it true that T must have a nontrivial invariant subspace, meaning a closed subspace M with M not equal to {0} or X and T(M) contained in M? The source records this broad Banach-space form as resolved negatively by counterexamples, including an operator on l^1 with no nontrivial invariant subspaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space, and let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. A closed subspace $M \subseteq X$ is called a nontrivial invariant subspace for $T$ if $M \neq \{0\}$, $M \neq X$, and $T(M) \subseteq M$. Determine whether the following statement is true: for every infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ and every bounded linear operator $T$ on $X$, the operator $T$ admits a nontrivial invariant subspace. Equivalently, decide whether there exists an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ and a bounded linear operator $T$ on $X$ such that the only closed subspaces $M \subseteq X$ with $T(M) \subseteq M$ are $M = \{0\}$ and $M = X$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Banach-space invariant subspace problem in this general form has been resolved negatively. P. Enflo (1976/1987) constructed a Banach space with a bounded operator having no nontrivial invariant subspace, and C. J. Read later produced a bounded operator on the classical Banach space $\ell^1$ with no nontrivial closed invariant subspaces.

status_evidence.title: On the invariant subspace problem for Banach spaces (Enflo)
status_evidence.snippet: Enflo's construction of a Banach space and operator with no nontrivial invariant subspace.
status_evidence.claim: The general Banach-space invariant subspace problem has a negative answer.

status_evidence.title: A solution to the invariant subspace problem on $\ell^1$ (Read)
status_evidence.snippet: C. J. Read constructed a bounded operator on $\ell^1$ with no nontrivial closed invariant subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: There exists a bounded operator on $\ell^1$ without nontrivial invariant subspaces.
